target_customer: Life science research labs that order custom oligonucleotides (DNA and RNA primers and probes) from outside suppliers
problem: Labs wait days for outsourced DNA synthesis. Kilobaser sells a desktop synthesizer using microfluidic chips and reagent cartridges so a lab can make oligos on the bench in under two hours.
business_model: Hardware instrument sales plus recurring cartridge and reagent sales
product_category: Benchtop DNA and RNA synthesizer (life science instruments)

founders.name: Alexander Murer
founders.role: Founder (later listed as CEO by Preqin)
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

founders.name: Martin Jost
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as molecular biologist, biohacker and full stack developer.

founders.name: Bernhard Tittelbach
founders.background_notes: YC bio lists interests in building things and running workshops; no education or employers given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining phosphoramidite synthesis chemistry, microfluidic chips, reagent cartridges and an instrument with a small team required hardware, chemistry and software at once.

defensibility.rationale: Instrument plus proprietary cartridges creates some lock-in and the engineering is hard to copy quickly, but benchtop synthesis was also being pursued by better funded firms later.

incumbents: Oligo suppliers such as Integrated DNA Technologies
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established by sources opened. Aggregator pages report a bankruptcy in July 2023 and an asset sale in January 2024, which would mean no incumbent copied it in time; this is unverified.

market_need_then: Life scientists routinely order primers and probes from outside vendors and wait for delivery. The YC description states that outsourcing stagnates research. No dated demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses kilobaser.com (exact .com). Acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, claims such as 'World's first plug and play synthesizer' and the YC line 'Nespresso Machine for DNA'

branding.brand_signature: Nespresso machine for DNA positioning (cartridge based desktop synthesizer)
branding.community_and_virality: Founder Tittelbach is active in maker and hacker circles per his YC bio. No press on the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name blends kilobase (a DNA length unit) and a suffix, which signals the field to scientists, and the Nespresso analogy is memorable. No evidence of wider brand awareness.

outcome_analysis: Kilobaser built a hard-tech desktop DNA synthesizer in Graz and joined YC in Winter 2021. Public funding data is thin: one aggregator shows an undisclosed round from Cathexis Ventures in April 2021 and about 125 thousand dollars total. CB Insights style listings report a bankruptcy filing in July 2023 and an asset sale in January 2024, but these come from aggregators only and the company website was still live, so the true status and cause are not public in sources I could verify. If the insolvency is real, long hardware development cycles with limited capital would be the likely pressure, which is inference only.
notes: YC lists the company as Active, but CB Insights and Preqin style aggregators report bankruptcy in July 2023 and an asset sale in January 2024; CB Insights returned 403 and could not be opened, so exit is recorded as unknown. Preqin lists a 15 July 2022 seed with SOSV (amount undisclosed) and Seedtable lists a 500K seed dated 2014-01 that looks like a placeholder; both are unverified single-aggregator claims and not recorded as rounds. The Nordic9 entry gives investor Cathexis Ventures and about 125K total received with no round amount. Founding year differs by source (2013 or 2014). Competitor search found only later or undated material (Dr. Oligo from Biolytic, DNA Script, Codex DNA now Telesis Bio, Evonetix, Catalog); none had a source dated near the Winter 2021 batch, so the list is left empty rather than guessed. The company site did not name founders or competitors.
